candidates.title: Anthropic pitches a federal AI safety bill that could block a model release

articles.title: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed

facts.fact: Politico reported that Anthropic has been circulating a draft AI safety bill it hopes Congress will consider.
A model's release could be blocked when there is a 'foreseeable, imminent risk' that over 50 people could die or over $1 billion in property damage could result.
The qualifying risk must stem from a biological weapon, the model evading its developer's controls, or a cyberattack.
The thresholds resemble those in California's Senate Bill 53, which recently became law.
The bill proposes independent evaluators registered with the U.S. Commerce Department, who could be paid by AI labs if payment is not contingent on their results.
If evaluators find an imminent catastrophic risk, they would have 72 hours to notify Commerce, which would ask a D.C. judge to halt the release.
The bill would bar federal agencies from halting a model's distribution on their own discretion.
Labs have mostly resisted mandatory government oversight, while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has argued the industry doesn't need new laws.

candidates.title: SpaceX's AI segment brings in $7.5B, 52% of revenue

articles.title: SpaceX's AI business is beating expectations

facts.fact: SpaceX reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue in a regulatory filing on Tuesday.
The renamed 'Super Intelligence' segment generated $7.5 billion in revenue; AI now makes up 52% of the company's income.
The AI business earned $431 million in profit, which would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one-time stock-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition.
Total capital expenditures were $19.6 billion; CFO Bret Johnsen said SpaceX would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter.
SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion versus a $1 billion loss in the same quarter last year, but still a $413 million net loss over the first nine months.
Starlink reached 13.6 million subscribers.
Musk predicted annual recurring revenue from Super Intelligence would reach 'somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion' by the end of 2027.
Musk said the next Starship test flight, expected in November, would attempt to recover both the booster and the second stage.

candidates.title: OpenAI buys biotech AI startup Orchestra Bio

articles.title: OpenAI acquires startup Orchestra Bio to beef up its biotech business

facts.fact: OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio, a four-year-old AI biotech software startup, announcing the deal on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.
The purchase price was not disclosed.
Orchestra reportedly raised about $20 million as of 2025 from Andreessen Horowitz, Atria and 8VC.
Orchestra builds AI agents that handle operational work for biotech companies, such as tracking finances and resolving clinical trial scheduling problems.
OpenAI is bringing Orchestra's team and technology into Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research.
Orchestra's work will also feed into Rosalind Workbench, a tool to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results.
OpenAI says Moderna and Novo Nordisk are among its Rosalind customers.

candidates.title: ChatGPT adds locked chats with PIN or Face ID

articles.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats

facts.fact: OpenAI announced on Oct. 20, 2026 that ChatGPT users can lock conversations to keep sensitive chats private when others may see their screen or device.
Locked chats are protected by a four-digit PIN, or Face ID or Touch ID on supported devices.
Unlike Temporary Chats, locked chats can be reopened at any time.
Locked chats move to a separate 'Locked Chats' section, apart from regular history, pinned chats and search results.
With Memory enabled, Locked Chats has its own memory that does not update regular Memory.
Locking does not add end-to-end encryption, change retention, or change the 'Improve the model for everyone' setting.
Resetting the PIN permanently deletes all locked chats, files and other content protected by the old PIN.
The feature covers Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu plans, and began rolling out Tuesday.

candidates.title: Microsoft: AI agents are like insider threats, launches Guardian Agents

articles.title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as 'frontier models can't be trusted'

facts.fact: Microsoft on October 19, 2026 introduced new security features to protect enterprises from the threat posed by AI agents.
The headline addition is Guardian Agents, for monitoring the AI agents a company uses; it is part of Project Perception, which launched in June.
Microsoft security business chief Hayete Gallot wrote that 'frontier models, regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted,' citing unpredictability rather than malice.
CEO Satya Nadella wrote: 'we need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.'
Microsoft Defender's new agent detection can identify up to 60 types of agents employees bring to work, including Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw.
New controls limit agents' access to data and systems and require human approval when an agent appears to be making risky decisions.
Microsoft was an inaugural member of Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform, backed by more than 100 other tech companies.
Microsoft also announced Surface Laptop Ultra PCs built for agents, running on Nvidia chips.

candidates.title: Otter.ai raises $320M without giving up equity

articles.title: Otter AI raises $320M from General Catalyst's growth fund for its meeting tool

facts.fact: Otter.ai announced on October 20, 2026 that it raised $320 million from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund, which offers capital without equity dilution and is tied to returns on marketing spend.
Otter has raised $50 million in total funding before this, with its last round in 2021, according to PitchBook.
Last year Otter passed $100 million in annual recurring revenue.
Otter says 40 million people have used its product, up from 25 million last year.
The money is planned for enterprise growth, go-to-market, international expansion and product innovation.
Otter is testing a prebrief feature and a Live Assist feature that lets users ask the AI questions during meetings.
Competitors include Fireflies.ai, Granola, Read AI and Circleback.

candidates.title: Robotics startup Eka hits $1.45B valuation with force-based robot model

articles.title: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving

facts.fact: Eka Robotics closed a $150 million Series A at a $1.45 billion post-money valuation, led by a16z and F-Prime.
It was founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja.
The robot handles about 1,500 objects weighing up to 1 kg in an hour, versus roughly 600 for a human, and reportedly succeeds more than 95% of the time.
Eka uses a vision-force-action model, centered on force inputs, rather than a vision-language-action design.
Its custom gripper has more force sensors than traditional grippers and costs under $1,000.
The gripper is rated for 5 million duty cycles, short of the 20 million target for standard industrial arms.
Eka trains with reinforcement learning in a physics simulator, producing thousands of hours of robot experience in minutes.
Eka runs undisclosed pilots with industrial customers; an outside professor flagged long-term reliability on real assembly lines as a key challenge.

candidates.title: Yelp's AI agent will phone restaurants to check wait times

articles.title: Yelp can now call on your behalf to check wait times at a restaurant

facts.fact: Yelp is adding a 'Check for Me' feature to restaurant pages where users enter party size and phone number.
